headline: Integrated gut microbiome and host-disease databases consolidate samples and multi-layer omics
label: Gut Microbiome Data Resources
summary: New NAR database releases pool 168 464 gut microbiome samples and host-microbe data across 15 gut-related diseases into reusable public resources.
synthesis: The dominant thread is consolidation of gut-related data into public databases. GutBiomeDB integrates human gut microbiome data from 168 464 samples, while gutDBase combines transcriptomic and microbial data from 175 bulk and single-cell datasets across 15 gut-related diseases, with interactive access. What distinguishes gutDBase is the joint organization of host transcriptomic and microbial layers across multiple disease contexts in one resource. The remaining items do not address the gut: R-loopBase v2.0 re-analyses 358 R-loop datasets from 16 technologies with quantitative confidence scoring, PmiREN3.0 is a multi-omics encyclopedia for plant microRNAs, and DeepHel is a multi-stage deep learning framework for Helitron annotation benchmarked on five eukaryotic genomes.
